classification.difficultyReason: Select the largest interval on which sine is one-to-one, then sketch the restricted function and its reflection.

content.prompt: The diagram shows $f(x)=\sin x$ in the domain $x\in[-\pi,\pi]$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10 supplied graph beneath the stem
spec.description: Sine curve on the closed interval from negative pi to pi, with positive-end axis arrows, six labelled ticks and no grid or endpoint markers.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the largest possible domain such that the inverse function exists.

answer.worked: The largest interval between turning points is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. On this interval, $\sin x$ is strictly increasing and therefore one-to-one. Include both turning points.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Sketch $y=f(x)$ with the restricted domain and $f^{-1}(x)$ on the same axis.

answer.short: Reflect the restricted sine curve in $y=x$. The inverse has endpoints $\left(-1,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$; both curves pass through $(0,0)$.
answer.worked: Sketch $y=\sin x$ for $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with endpoints $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$. Reflect the curve in $y=x$, interchanging the coordinates of each point. The inverse has endpoints $\left(-1,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Both curves pass through $(0,0)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Supplied answer sketch below question 10 part b
spec.description: Restricted sine in blue and its inverse in red, with filled endpoints, complete endpoint labels, coloured dashed projection guides and a dashed reflection line.
spec.mathematics: Blue: y=sin(x), -pi/2<=x<=pi/2. Red: reflection parametrised by (sin(t),t), -pi/2<=t<=pi/2. Dashed line y=x. Both curves pass through the origin.
